svg.title: Heart rate over one climb, averaged across 16 seeds
svg.desc: The mean heart rate of sixteen simulated runs aligned on the foot of a climb, from five minutes before it to the crest. Heart rate sits at a settled 166.6 bpm on the flat approach, rises once the climb begins and levels off at a plateau of 178.9 bpm, a rise of 12.3 bpm. It covers 63 per cent of that rise, reaching 174.3 bpm, 104 seconds after the foot of the climb. The line is an ensemble mean because on any single run the crossing time ranges from 0 to 290 seconds, which reflects where the noise sat rather than physiology. There is no published field reference for this measurement, so none is drawn.
